In Virginia a 'spoiled' ballot is a absentee ballot that the voter decided not to use but showed up at the poll with the ballot in hand and requested to vote in person. The absentee ballot was then marked 'SPOILED' and put in a special envelop with any other 'spoiled' ballots that were turned in.
The 'spoiled' ballots are counted after the polls close and added to the poll tally sheet. If you were sent an absentee ballot, the registration system would show the voter had been issued an absentee ballot and therefore could not vote again unless the absentee ballot was turned in and disqualified by marking it 'spoiled' at which time the voter would be issued a new ballot for 'in person' voting.

If the person was issued an absentee ballot, but claimed not to have used it and did not bring it to the poll, they could be issued a 'provisional ballot' that would be counted after all the election results were in and the determination made by the County Registrar that the absentee ballot had not, in fact, been used.

Provisional ballots were also accounted for and added to the poll tally so that all ballots cast or spoiled during the hours of the election were accounted for.

Throwing away 'spoiled ballots' would cause your total vote tally to be off.
